bioconda.name: vepyr
bioconda.summary: Rust-powered Ensembl VEP variant annotation for Python.
bioconda.description:
vepyr (VEP Yielding Performant Results) is a Python interface to a Rust
reimplementation of Ensembl's Variant Effect Predictor, built on Apache
Arrow and DataFusion. It converts Ensembl VEP caches to Parquet and
annotates variants through a streaming engine, returning Polars LazyFrames
or annotated VCF files.

commands: python -c "import vepyr; assert vepyr.__version__ == '0.10.0'; targets = vepyr.supported_vep_targets(); assert targets; assert all(t.get('vepyr_version') == '0.10.0' for t in targets); assert {t.get('cache_version') for t in targets} == {'115', '116'}; print('compiled VEP targets passed')"

python -c "import tempfile; from pathlib import Path; from vepyr._core import vcf_contigs; tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(); vcf = Path(tmp.name) / 'smoke.vcf'; vcf.write_text('##fileformat=VCFv4.2
#CHROM	POS	ID	REF	ALT	QUAL	FILTER	INFO
1	101	.	A	G	.	PASS	.
2	202	.	C	T	.	PASS	.
'); contigs = tuple(sorted(vcf_contigs(str(vcf)))); assert contigs == ('1', '2'), contigs; tmp.cleanup(); print('native VCF scan passed')"
